scope: Trace the citations that ECW-308 (Wang et al., Adv. Funct. Mater. 2023, 10.1002/adfm.202212342) uses for the G1+ target compounds back to the cited documents, and classify each cited document as primary measurement, journal-reported value, or secondary compilation.

request_accounting.policy: read-only; no Sci-Hub; no paywall bypass; no proxy

evidence_policy.reported_integer_values: ECW-308 writes two decimals where the cited table reports integers; the extra precision is attributed to ECW-308 and not to the source.
evidence_policy.closed_dois_not_added_to_source_dois_all: A single dataset row can only carry one licence metadata set, so a second differently-licensed source is recorded in notes only.

cited_documents.citation: Y. Huang, L. Zhao, L. Li, M. Xie, F. Wu, R. Chen, Adv. Mater. 2019, 31, 1808393.

access.publisher: Wiley landing page, Crossref full-xml and SI endpoint all returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare)

cited_documents.consequence: The diglyme and triglyme entries in ECW-308 are third-hand relays; they were recorded as consistency checks only.

cited_documents.citation: B. Flamme, G. Rodriguez Garcia, M. Weil, M. Haddad, P. Phansavath, V. Ratovelomanana-Vidal, et al., Green Chem. 2017, 19, 1828.

access.rsc: landing page and articlehtml returned HTTP 403; standard SI paths returned HTTP 404

cited_documents.consequence: No evidence that Flamme 2017 performed the PC or EC dielectric measurements; it cannot be promoted to primary.

cited_documents.citation: H. Duncan, N. Salem, Y. Abu-Lebdeh, J. Electrochem. Soc. 2013, 160, A838.
cited_documents.method_statement: Dielectric constant measurements of solvents and mixtures were carried out using BI-870 dielectric constant Meter from Brookhaven Instruments.
cited_documents.limitation: Table I carries no per-row provenance, so it cannot be established which entries are this paper's own measurements and which are comparison values; temperature, frequency and uncertainty are absent. VC 126.00 and FEC 78.40 do not appear in the text.
cited_documents.consequence: The adiponitrile and glutaronitrile conflicts are now against a peer-reviewed article, and the two decimals in ECW-308 are unsupported precision.

cited_documents.citation: D. S. Hall, A. Eldesoky, E. R. Logan, E. M. Tonita, X. Ma, J. R. Dahn, J. Electrochem. Soc. 2018, 165, A2365.

licence.name: CC BY 4.0
licence.evidence: Stated in the article itself, and independently in OpenAlex W2885314186 and Semantic Scholar (openAccessPdf license=CCBY)

cited_documents.access: IOP serves the article behind a Radware bot manager hCaptcha; after the human challenge was confirmed the CC-BY article and Table I were read in full.

table.label: Table I
table.temperature_note: Values are shown for 25 C or as noted; footnote c states that the viscosity and permittivity values for EC are at 40 C.

reported_values.note: ref 78 is the same DOI as this repository's EC primary source, so the loop corroborates the 313.15 K assignment rather than adding an independent measurement

cited_documents.citation: A. H. Saadi, W. H. Lee, J. Chem. Soc. B 1966, 5-6.
cited_documents.title: Physicochemical studies of some cyclic carbonates. Part V. The alkaline hydrolysis of vinylene carbonate
cited_documents.reached_via: ECW-308 citation [3] -> Hall 2018 Table I ref 82
cited_documents.abstract_quote: The dielectric constant and dipole moment of vinylene carbonate have been measured, and the alkaline hydrolysis of this ester in dilute aqueous ethanol has been studied. This reaction is first-order in ester concentration, and k1=0.067 sec-1 at 25. A mechanism for the hydrolysis is proposed.

access.rsc: Article landing page served to the institutional session (Wuhan University); the two-page full text is paywalled and no first-page numeric table was rendered

cited_documents.limitation: The abstract confirms that the dielectric constant of vinylene carbonate was measured, but the numeric value could not be read, so the row is not promoted to primary.
